title: Custom 'bind' Polyfill with 'new' Operator Support
concept: Currying, Prototype Chaining, and new.target Resolution
problemStatement: Implement `Function.prototype.myBind(thisArg, ...outerArgs)`. It must support partial application (currying), and when the bound function is invoked as a constructor using `new BoundFn()`, the provided `thisArg` MUST be ignored and a new instance inheriting from the original function's prototype must be created.
interviewTrap: 90% of candidates miss the `new` operator rule: when a bound function is called with `new`, the bound `thisArg` is completely ignored in favor of the newly instantiated object.

testCases.name: Standard bound invocation with curried arguments
testCases.testFn: function add(a, b) { return a + b; } const add10 = add.myBind(null, 10); return add10(20);

testCases.name: Maintains object this context
testCases.testFn: const user = { name: 'Alex' }; function getName() { return this.name; } return getName.myBind(user)();

testCases.name: Supports 'new' operator correctly overriding thisArg
testCases.testFn: function Point(x, y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; } const BoundPoint = Point.myBind({ x: 99 }, 5); const pt = new BoundPoint(10); return { x: pt.x, y: pt.y, isInstance: pt instanceof Point };

details.name: Standard bound invocation with curried arguments

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A complete polyfill for `Function.prototype.myBind` must not only bind `this` and partially apply arguments (currying), but also support being used with the `new` operator. When a bound function is constructed (`new boundFn()`), the bound `this` must be IGNORED and a fresh instance of the original constructor must be created instead.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Check if called via `new`: `this instanceof bound` (or `new.target`).
If called via `new`, use `this` (the newly instantiated object); otherwise, use the originally supplied `boundThis`.
Inherit prototype chain: Set `bound.prototype = Object.create(targetFn.prototype)` so instances pass `instanceof targetFn` checks.
Execute `targetFn.apply(effectiveThis, allArgs)` and return result (handling constructor object returns).
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: ECMA-262 §10.4.1.1 specifies `[[Construct]]` on Bound Function Exotic Objects. When constructed via `new`, the bound function delegates to the original constructor's `[[Construct]]`, completely bypassing `[[BoundThis]]`. Our polyfill replicates this specification requirement faithfully.

complexity.time: O(1) creation; O(1) dispatch per call.
complexity.space: O(A) space for bound arguments array.

edgeCasesHandled: Constructor usage (`new boundFn()`) ignores `boundThis` and instantiates target prototype.
Partial application (currying) combines initial arguments with runtime arguments.
Instanceof operator works for both bound and original constructor.

specifications: ECMA-262 §10.4.1.1 [[Construct]] on Bound Function Exotic Objects
